profile.summary: tomduncalf is a Mid-Level JavaScript developer with specialized expertise in Chart.js, focusing on data visualization, time-series charting, and UX-driven feature enhancements. Their contributions demonstrate deep knowledge of JavaScript APIs, time-based data handling, and visual rendering optimizations. While primarily frontend-focused, their work aligns with developers building interactive dashboards or analytics tools. The contributions show strong problem-solving skills in debugging rendering issues and extending library functionality while maintaining backward compatibility.
skill_evidence: PR #1: Fixed gradient color parsing error in Chart.js color helpers, demonstrating debugging of complex rendering logic and CSS/JS color system knowledge.
PR #2: Corrected `userCallback` behavior for time axes, showing deep understanding of callback patterns and asynchronous data handling in time-series charts.
PR #3: Added `minRotation` option for angular scaling, indicating familiarity with canvas-based rendering and user-controlled chart interactions.
PR #4: Implemented `isoWeekday` for aligning grid lines with Wednesday-based data, proving expertise in JavaScript `Date` object and ISO standards.
PR #5: Introduced `labelOffset` with visual comparison screenshots, highlighting UX-focused feature development and attention to visual clarity.
PR descriptions mention 'works for my use case' but also note limitations, showing awareness of real-world constraints and API design trade-offs.
All PRs involve extending Chart.js’s public API with new configurable options, demonstrating intentional API design and backward compatibility considerations.
The `isoWeekday` PR references business cycle alignment, suggesting familiarity with how data visualization should align with real-world scheduling patterns.
